subject: 48768953025E40D1B1F978FF61180A24
introduction: “If two souls quarrel and contend about a question of the divine questions, differing and disputing, both are wrong.” Bahá’u’lláh forbade religious contention outright, and ‘Abdu’l-Bahá explained why: the purpose of religion is love, and a truth won in a quarrel has lost its purpose. One is to state one’s understanding with kindness and, if it is not accepted, leave the other person alone. The pastoral letters say the same, “the servant of the Lord must not strive”, and the Qur’an’s “reason with them in the better way” is the method. Jude’s “earnestly contend for the faith”, Paul’s confrontation with Peter, Milton’s grappling of truth and falsehood and Blake’s “contraries” are the claims of argument.
questions: What is the difference between disagreeing and contending?
“Both are wrong.” How can someone who is right about the matter be wrong?
Paul opposed Peter to his face. Would the readings have had him keep silent?
How does a community that avoids dispute keep from avoiding thought?

outside.why: Contend not with anyone. If it be possible, as much as lieth in you, live peaceably with all men.
If you possess a truth another lacks, share it in kindliness. Be ready always to give an answer, with meekness and fear.
If it be refused, leave him to himself. Unto you your religion, and unto me my religion.
The most negligent is he who disputes idly. The beginning of strife is as when one letteth out water: therefore leave off contention, before it be meddled with.
Let not corrupt inclination provoke divisions. From whence come wars and fightings among you? come they not hence, even of your lusts?
It is not permissible to contend, nor to ill-treat. A soft answer turneth away wrath.
Shun every form of dispute; utter the Word, and if refused, leave it. The servant of the Lord must not strive; but be gentle unto all men.
Jude wrote to the same churches that ye should earnestly contend for the faith which was once delivered unto the saints. Is there a contending the readings would permit?
The friends delivered from argument. Paul over a matter of principle: when Peter was come to Antioch, I withstood him to the face, because he was to be blamed. When is open disagreement a duty?
Explain with love and kindness, not harshness. Reason with them in the better way.
Beware lest you engage in opposing views and conflicting beliefs. Do all things without murmurings and disputings.
Some acclaim Christ as God, others as the Word, others as a prophet: shall they fight over it? That there should be no schism in the body.
If two souls quarrel over a divine question, both are wrong. Franklin’s rule: to forbear all direct contradiction to the sentiments of others, and all positive assertion of my own.
Contention even over the Cause itself is forbidden. Blake: without contraries is no progression. Can a community that forbids dispute still think?
People forgot the foundation and clung to points of difference. Ye have omitted the weightier matters of the law.
Milton trusted open argument to bring out the truth. The readings trust consultation and forbid contention. What is the difference between the two, in practice?

shortfall: Eighty further readings repeat the prohibition of dispute in other words and settings; companions and objections were set once.
